newsitem.title: UKRAINE: Ukraine's Kuchma sacks finance, economy ministers.
newsitem.headline: Ukraine's Kuchma sacks finance, economy ministers.

text.p: Ukrainian President Leonid Kuchma sacked his finance minister on Tuesday along with three other ministers with economic and industrial portfolios, his press service said.
"Finance Minister Valentyn Koronevsky has been sacked for serious inadequacies in his work," it said in a statement issued to Reuters.

Statistics Minister Olexander Osaulenko had been sacked for bad management while Economy Minister Vasyl Hureyev and the minister for machine-building and the military complex, Valery Maleyev, were moved to other posts.
Kuchma, on holiday in western Ukraine, signed the decrees following a request from the cabinet, it added.
The Ukrainian leader has often spoken of the need for changes in the ministries in recent months, particularly those working on economic issues.
He started off the process by sacking his agriculture minister and deputy transport minister at the first meeting of a new anti-corruption body earlier this month.
Ukrainian media have speculated that Prime Minister Pavlo Lazarenko, whose criticism of the four men appeared to spark Tuesday's sackings, might himself be at risk of losing his job.
Lazarenko sharply criticised the work of the ministries at a cabinet meeting on Friday and Western analysts said he appeared to be trying to deflect criticism from himself.
"It all depends whether this will be enough to satisfy his critics," said one analyst when asked if Lazarenko was secure.

Lazarenko faces constant criticism -- by conservatives for unpaid wages, by reformers for this year's budget draft and by industrialists who say a new package of tax laws fails to support domestic producers.

Deputy Prime Minister Viktor Pynzenyk, in charge of economic reform in the former Soviet republic, told reporters on Saturday that he had no information on sackings but that the cabinet had to consist of a group of people who could "play in tune."
A huge mountain of unpaid wages has accumulated in Ukraine, standing at 4.2 billion hryvnias ($2.3 billion) at the start of the year from three billion hryvnias in the middle of last year.
Meanwhile gross domestic product fell by 10.4 percent in January year-on-year. $ = 1.8150 hryvnias
